The long-word chunking and returning [] for blank input are correct fixes. They make test_long_words_are_split, test_width_of_one and test_blank_text_gives_no_lines pass.

But the PR also changes the packing check from `<= width` to `< width`. That contradicts the docstring, which says a word is added "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long". Joined lines can now never reach exactly `width`, even though a single chunk can. Only test_meeting_reminder needs this change: at width 20, "The meeting has" + " been" is exactly 20 characters, so the documented rule gives "The meeting has been", but the test expects "The meeting has". Every other test passes with `<=`.

So the test and the docstring disagree, and the PR quietly bent the implementation to match the test without saying so. It has no description and doesn't update the docstring. Please restore `<=` and raise the test_meeting_reminder vs. docstring conflict with the teammate or the notifications team. Either that expected output is wrong, or the spec really is "strictly less than width" and the docstring and README need to say so explicitly. Please also add a PR description explaining the change.
